text:
elaine: heads-up — I opened a tiny PR to add a minimal 'reserved pool' provisioning example and a short autoscale cooldown note. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4921

aj: looks good, can you add an SDK snippet for the Python client? customers keep asking for a quick copy-paste.

elaine: yes — added a placeholder in the PR description, wanted to run it by y'all. here's the snippet I sketched:

elaine: ```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
resp = client.create_capacity(
    tenant_id="acme-tenant",
    pool={
        "gpu_type": "a100-40gb",
        "min_instances": 2,
        "max_instances": 10,
        "isolation": "tenant"
    },
    autoscale={"cooldown_seconds": 180, "scale_up_threshold": 0.7}
)
print(resp)
```

sam: small nit — in SDK examples we prefer `min_replicas`/`max_replicas` naming (internally we map to instances). please keep parity with existing client API. also the `isolation` enum is `tenant_level` now.

elaine: good catch. updating.

michael: SLA phrasing: the doc currently says "best-effort warm start" which sounds soft. Could we instead say "warm start is best-effort; cold starts may incur additional latency" — a little clearer for customers.

elaine: yes, I can change that line. any legal/enterprise wording we should flag?

prashant: pinging infra: on the cooldown example, the number 180 is fine but we should show a quick rationale comment — e.g., "short cooldown -> faster scale up, but may oscillate under bursty traffic."

elaine: adding a one-liner rationale.

aj: think about adding a tiny troubleshooting tip under "provisioning failures" — common cause: tenant label mismatch. Like: `check tenant labels on TF resource and Dedicated API`. keeps support ops tickets down.

elaine: done in a follow-up commit.

sam: link fix request — the PR references the 'isolation heuristics' page with an old path. new path is /docs/ops/provisioning/isolation-heuristics.html.

elaine: updated link in PR.

docs-bot: CI passed on docs build (link: https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/43211).

michael: quick review: lgtm except for the SDK naming and the SLA wording tweak.

sam: I'll submit a tiny patch to the Python snippet while I'm reviewing.

prashant: one more ask — can we include a short YAML manifest example for Terraform users? 1-2 lines showing the tenant binding.

elaine: added a tiny YAML example in the provisioning section:```yaml
resource "redwood_reserved_pool" "acme" {
  tenant = "acme-tenant"
  gpu_type = "a100-40gb"
  min_replicas = 2
}
```

aj::+1: looks cleaner now.

sam: merging after small checks — will apply the SDK rename and SLA wording in a follow-up commit on the same PR.

elaine: thanks everyone. I'll backfill a tiny test-case for the example in our docs smoke tests.

michael: can you also add a changelog note in the dedicated docs release notes? one line: "added reserved-pool example and autoscale cooldown guidance".

elaine: done. updated the release notes section in the PR.

prashant: cheers. tagging support@ for awareness.

elaine: tagging done. closing loop — will ping once the SDK PR patch lands. :party_popper:
